1.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Krishna Kant Yadav, learned counsel for applicant, Sri P.K. Giri, learned Additional Advocate General assisted by Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material available on record.

3. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.148 of 2023, under Sections 376(3), 354-A IPC, Section 4(2) POCSO Act and Section 3(2)5 of SC/ST Act, Police Station Meerganj, District Bareilly with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

sentences.text: The applicant is stated to have committed aggravated sexual assault with the daughter of the informant aged about 17 years on 02.06.2023 at about 5:30 p.m.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
6. The FIR is delayed by about five hours and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
7. The victim and the informant have not supported the prosecution story during their cross-examination, although they have supported the story during their examination-in-chief.

8. The medical report also does not support the prosecution story as it stands falsified by the statement of the victim during her cross-examination, whereby she has stated that she was having periods at that time as such she had rubbed her vital part and got injured.
9. The applicant is languishing in jail since 04.06.2023, as such his fundamental rights enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated.
There is no likelihood of conclusion of trial in near future as it is moving at a snail's pace.
More than one year have passed since his incarceration and only two witnesses of fact have been examined.
Even the informant has not been examined.
There is no criminal history of the applicant and he is ready to cooperate with trial.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE BY A.G.A.:
10. The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the prosecution story stands corroborated by the injury report itself.
11. The victim and her mother, who has been examined as PW-2, have supported the prosecution story during their examination-in-chief.
12. The injury report categorically says that there are signs suggestive of recent penetration of vagina.

The doctor conducting medical examination of the victim has found redness at labia majora,
labia minora,fourchette and introitus and has also observed that the hymen was freshly torn and had clots on it, as such the applicant is not entitled for bail.

13. The said defence by the applicant that the victim was undergoing period at the time of offence stands falsified from the fact that the said fact has not been observed by the doctor at the time of her medical examination.
He has stated that the last menstruation period was on 03.05.2023 that was about one month before the occurrence.

CONCLUSION:
14. After hearing the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the medical examination of the victim, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.

16. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously as early as possible in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Apex Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
